assignments.reason: This concept IS holy malkhut in a specific state — exile (galut). Its essential nature is malkhut deKedushah, the kingdom of holiness. The galut is a condition of that kingdom, not a separate domain. It belongs with the holy-malkhut/neginah cluster because the text says 'now malkhut deKedushah is in exile, therefore the neginah is damaged' — the subject is malkhut itself.

The damaged neginah is still neginah in its essence — it is the holy music in a state of impairment caused by the exile of malkhut. Its essential nature is music/neginah, the core concept of Package 1. It describes what happens to holy music when its source (malkhut deKedushah) is in galut.

The cantors lacking da'at is the human-level expression of the damaged neginah. The text states explicitly that because malkhut deKedushah is in exile, the cantors cannot draw their music from its holy root (mochin/da'at of malkhut deKedushah). The essential nature of this concept is the chazan/musician domain — Package 1 already contains חזן and מנגן. This is the cantor in the current impaired state.

assignments.node_id: מי שהוא כשר, נמשכת הנגינה שלו
assignments.reason: This concept describes the righteous musician whose music draws from the two holy birds — the essential nature is holy neginah as it manifests through a worthy person. It is about the quality of the music and its holy source, placing it squarely in the holy-music/malkhut domain.

Hearing music from a kosher and worthy musician — the essential nature is the act of receiving holy neginah. The Torah's opening proposition: when you hear from a kosher musician, it is good. This is the positive reception of holy music, belonging to the holy-neginah domain.

The 'good' that results from hearing holy music is the spiritual benefit of holy neginah. In the Torah's framework, this is the positive outcome within the holy-music domain — it describes the state of being aligned with holy malkhut through music. Its essential nature is the goodness inherent in the holy-neginah system.

Hearing the neginah is the act of receiving holy music that leads to building malkhut. The text says 'through hearing the neginah, one repairs the building of his malkhut.' The essential nature is the act of receiving neginah — it belongs in the neginah/malkhut domain.

Repairing the building of one's malkhut is essentially the concept of binyan hamalkhut — the building of the kingdom, which is already a core node in Package 1. This is the active/dynamic form of the same concept: constructing holy malkhut.

The elevation and completion of neginah describes the eschatological perfection of holy music — when malkhut deKedushah is elevated, the music will be complete in the aspect of da'at of holy malkhut. Its essential nature is the fulfillment of holy neginah.

This node (text: 'nitale malkhut deKedushah') refers to the elevation of holy malkhut. It IS malkhut deKedushah in its essence — the same core concept of Package 1. The edge describes how repairing non-holy music leads to the elevation of holy malkhut, and how the future elevation of malkhut leads to the completion of neginah.

The act of repairing non-holy music and elevating it to holiness is a redemptive action belonging to the holy-malkhut domain. David HaMelech exemplifies this — his ability to take music from 'behind holiness' and elevate it. The essential nature is tikkun (repair) within the holy-neginah system, not the evil music itself.

The ability to hear neginah from any person — even from a wicked musician — without harm is the perfected state of the holy-neginah system. It is the tikkun's goal: immunity to evil music through the holy framework. Its essential nature is the holy capacity for receiving music.

The 'place where prophets nurse' is the spiritual source of the holy birds and of prophecy/neginah. Package 1 already contains נבואה (prophecy) and the two holy birds. This concept IS the source-location of prophecy — the same domain. The Zohar states the holy birds nurse from this place, making it the root of the entire holy-neginah structure.

The tikkun (repair) of the kaneh (windpipe/reed) is the repair of the physical instrument of voice/music. The kaneh is the instrument through which neginah flows, and its repair is what enables the cherubim to be face-to-face. The essential nature is the holy-music apparatus — the physical dimension of the neginah/malkhut system.

The 'rising of the song' (tekumah larinah) from the verse 'kumi roni balailah' represents the restoration of holy neginah. The essential nature is the song/music itself being restored — it IS neginah in its resurrected state. While it is achieved through night-learning, the concept itself is about the music.

The 'breasts of the malkhut' (dadei hamalkhut) in the Zohar's statement refers to the impure malkhut from which the klipah-birds suckle. This is not the holy malkhut — it is the malkhut of the sitra achra that nourishes evil music. The text says 'the birds of the klipah suckle from the breasts of malkhut' — this malkhut is the evil kingdom that feeds the evil-music system.

assignments.node_id: כשהמנגן הוא רשע, אזי הוא לוקח הנגינה שלו
assignments.reason: The wicked musician taking his music from the klipah-birds — this is the evil-music process itself. The essential nature is the evil musician operating within the klipah system. Package 3 is the evil-music/klipah-birds domain, and this is the human agent within that evil system.

Hearing music from a wicked musician is the act of receiving evil neginah. The Torah states this is harmful to serving God. Its essential nature is the evil-music experience — the listener's encounter with klipah-sourced music. It belongs in the evil mirror of Package 1.

Difficulty in serving God is the effect of evil music on the listener. Its essential nature is the spiritual damage caused by the klipah-music system — the harm that evil neginah inflicts. It is the evil-domain consequence, the mirror of 'tov lo' (good for him) in the holy domain.

The snake swallowing the holy music represents the forces of evil consuming holiness. The nachash (snake/serpent) is the classic symbol of the sitra achra. This concept belongs to the evil domain — it IS the destructive action of the klipah upon holy music. The snake is the agent of evil within this Torah's narrative.

Learning not for its own sake (shelo lishmah) — the essential nature is a mode of Torah learning. It IS a kind of learning, specifically learning 'in order to be called Rabbi.' While its effect is negative (the learning is diminished, the snake swallows it), the concept itself is about Torah study in a flawed state. It belongs in the Torah/learning domain (Package 2) because it IS learning, just improperly motivated.

The diminished importance of learning — this describes the state of Torah study when done shelo lishmah. Its essential nature is a quality of limud (learning), placing it in the Torah/learning domain. It is not evil per se — it is Torah learning in a diminished state, making it neutral rather than evil.

The act of learning shelo lishmah (in the Talmudic narrative, 'Rabbah is saying it' = learning to be called Rabbi). This is functionally the same concept as כשלומד שלא לשמה — a mode of Torah learning. Its essential nature is Torah study in an imperfect motivation, belonging to the learning domain.

Learning at night — this IS night-learning, the central practice of Package 2. The Torah states that learning at night draws a thread of chesed upon the learner. Its essential nature is Torah study at night, the core activity of the laylah/oral-Torah domain.

Learning Oral Torah at night — this is the explicit tikkun (remedy) the Torah prescribes. It is Torah she-be'al peh (already in Package 2) combined with laylah (already in Package 2). Its essential nature is the practice of night-learning of the Oral Torah.

Learning the Shas (Talmud/sixty tractates) — the text explicitly equates Shas with Gemara, which IS laylah (night). 'Through learning Shas one repairs the six rings of the kaneh.' The essential nature is Talmud study, which is Package 2's core identity (Gemara = laylah = Torah she-be'al peh).

Repairing the six rings of the kaneh — while the kaneh itself belongs to the music domain, the SIX rings (שית עיזקאין) correspond to the sixty tractates (שתין בתי) of the Shas. The text explicitly links שית עיזקאין to שתין מסכתות. The additions file already placed שית עיזקאין שבקנה in Package 2 as a bechina of קול. This action-node (repairing them) shares the same essential nature.

assignments.node_id: חוט של חסד נמשך עליו (ג) ומגן עליו שלא יזיק לו המחשבה הנ"ל
assignments.reason: The thread of chesed being drawn upon the learner and protecting him — this is the active manifestation of chesed/Abraham/tree. The additions file already placed חוט של חסד in Package 4. This longer-form node describes the same reality: the protective chesed-thread that shields against evil thought. Its essential nature is chesed as protection.

The thread of chesed drawn upon him — this is the same chesed-thread concept. The Maharsha interprets the tree (ilan) as Abraham = chesed, and the thread of chesed is what flows from that tree to protect. Its essential nature is the chesed of Abraham, the core of Package 4.

Protection from the snake — this is the active defensive function of the chesed/Abraham/tree system. Rabbah marvels at how great the power of the tree (chesed) is, that it can protect even one who learns shelo lishmah. The essential nature is the protective power of chesed, not the snake itself. It describes what chesed DOES.
